rule: Phase B review findings, continuing Phase A's RV sequence (RV-01..RV-53 are in the frozen phase-a review register). Each finding names what was wrong, the fix, and where the fix is proven. Reviewer: the session itself (the no-agents rule); your review follows.

findings.finding: Nothing tied the library's tier-field tuples (digests.REQUIREMENT_FIELDS / CONTRACT_FIELDS / RECORD_FIELDS) or the frozen V-A preimage shapes to Chapter 0's identity.json. A drift (a field added to a tuple, a preimage built from the wrong subset) would pass every existing check because the goldens and the library would drift together.
findings.fix: New checker check identity.tiers_match: (a) the three tuples must equal the top-level heads of identity.json's tier field paths exactly; (b) the frozen V-A canonical preimages must contain exactly the expected keys (all requirement heads; the 12 contract heads plus requirement_digest; the record heads minus the absent supersession_provenance plus contract_digest). A planted defect (a key removed from the frozen requirement preimage) proves the check bites.

findings.finding: Freeze misclassification: a delegated contract whose repository_id is outside the delegation's repository_ids was REJECTED, because the SEM-10 floor-entry equality (which resolves the floor from mandatory_floors[repo][class] and finds no entry) fired as a hard issue before the SEM-11 repository check could queue it. Chapter 0 routes outside-delegation work to you (t-c04 QUEUED_FOR_YOU), not to rejection (t-c07 is for unresolved inputs, unbound assertions and location mismatches).
findings.fix: validate_freeze now evaluates the floor-entry equality only when the repository is among the delegation's repository_ids; outside it, the repository finding queues and the floor subset/hash checks still hold. New freeze case: declaration and contract for a repository the delegation does not cover now dispose QUEUED_FOR_YOU.

findings.finding: A registration's entrypoint accepted dot segments: the schema's coarse pattern allowed '../escape.py' and no grammar walk covered the field, so a closure-relative entrypoint could point outside the closure. INV-66 makes the closure the only thing a frozen contract may execute; an escaping entrypoint undercuts exactly that.
findings.fix: entrypoint is validated as a D-26 RepoPath (no '.', '..', backslash, empty segments; root spelling not allowed) by the path walk for both registration kinds; a traversal negative is in the schema suite.

findings.finding: Chapter 0 does not order t-c03 (duplicate) against t-c04 (queue-for-you) when both preconditions hold for one payload. The library classifies duplicate first; that reading was silent.
findings.fix: Recorded in the P-2 resolution note and the admission docs: a payload matching a live ContractDigest without force_new_sequence is a DUPLICATE regardless of scope findings, because INV-54 says it creates no record and no Sequence — there is nothing for you to approve. The precedence is a stated Chapter 1 reading, reversible by a Chapter 0 correction if you want queue-first.

findings.finding: SEM-09 could be mistaken for lineage integrity. It only enforces that a contract's delegation_id equals the bound record's field; whether every record of one delegation carries the same delegation_id is the authority service's minting rule, not checkable from a contract.
findings.fix: obj-00's representation obligations now state the boundary: lineage constancy is Chapter 8's minting rule; Chapter 1 enforces copy-consistency only (D-44).

findings.finding: Count defects in the consolidated review: it claimed 36 schema negatives when 35 existed, and the checker's planted-defect count changed when the review added cases.
findings.fix: RV-56's new negative makes 36 true; the checker suite is 19 planted defects plus the control; the review restates both from the run output, not from memory.

findings.finding: SEM-04's statement promised more than the code enforces: it said the mode 'must be consistent with the declaration's publication_mode', but in v1 no mode/publication_mode combination is a freeze rejection — a MEDIATED-bound source contract freezes and waits at BLOCKED_UNSUPPORTED_FINALIZER (INV-64, t-s04). The enforced parts are: mode requires REMOTE, and READ_ONLY forbids a mode.
findings.fix: SEM-04's statement now says exactly what is enforced and names INV-64 as the READY-gate owner of publication-mode fit, matching D-54's wording.
